capital: None. No permanent residents; research stations only.

transport: No airports for tourists and no hotels. Almost all visitors sail from Ushuaia, Argentina (about 2 days across the Drake Passage), or fly from Punta Arenas in Chile on air-cruise trips. From India you fly via a Gulf or European hub to Buenos Aires, then on to Ushuaia. Season runs November to March. About USD 7,200 to 15,800 for 10 to 11 day Peninsula cruises on operator listings from late 2026 (roughly 6 to 14 lakh rupees), with flights, visa and insurance extra. Last-minute deals appear in Ushuaia, but cabins also sell out.

cautions: No visa is needed for Antarctica itself, but you need a valid passport to board, plus the visa for Argentina or Chile where you start (both need one for Indians, with exceptions for some US visa holders).
Permits are issued to tour operators under the Antarctic Treaty, so cruise passengers do not apply themselves. Whether Indian law adds a separate requirement for Indian citizens was not verified.

Travel insurance with emergency evacuation is required. Wildlife rules apply: no sitting, kneeling or leaving equipment near animals, boots washed between landings (bird flu precautions). Ships with more than 500 passengers may not land anyone.

visa.rule: Antarctica is not a country and has no visa. Visitors need a valid passport and a permit that their tour operator holds under the Antarctic Treaty. No vaccinations are required. You need a visa for the country you sail from: Argentina (Ushuaia, 90-day tourist visa, apply online or at the Argentine embassy in New Delhi at least 4 weeks ahead) or Chile (Punta Arenas).
visa.note: Probable, not final. Based on operator and guide sites, not an official page. Confirm with your operator and the Argentine or Chilean embassy.
